scope: Regional and joint remainder-density estimates under the actual SU2 Wilson law. For any finite edge region B, the actual conditional partition is bounded below by exp(-C_B), where C_B=(6*beta*epsilon_K-log(massLower_K))*|B|+4*beta*|boundary B| and epsilon_K is the proved Haar-cap squared tolerance. The boundary consists of plaquettes touching both B and its complement. Exact cancellation removes all untouched plaquettes from the normalized conditional law, uniformly in every frozen exterior. The exponential moment of sqrt(beta)/2 times the sum over B of sqrt(R_e) is at most exp(C_B), both conditionally and under the original interacting Wilson law, with no total-volume normalization penalty. At t_B=(2/3)*q(beta)+8*sqrt(beta)*|boundary B|/|B|+2/sqrt(beta), P(D_B>=t_B)<=exp(-|B|), where D_B is the regional mean square-root remainder. For any finite family of nonempty disjoint edge regions, the joint event is bounded by exp(-sum |B_i|), without independence of their events. If beta*|boundary B_i|<=|B_i| for every region, the same joint bound holds at one common threshold u(beta)=(2/3)*q(beta)+10/sqrt(beta) tending to zero. This proves a regional energy/normalization and specified joint-event bound, not a count over all contours, control of every microscopic bad cluster, repeated-scale interaction estimates, retained-sector correlation bounds or a continuum limit.
